context:
Goal: the git copy of the waiting page is never older than your last save.
Problem (goal): you asked "shd me hitting send on an artifact be another update trigger". Today Send already wakes the page's writer (triage); the git copy is exported only when triage chooses to, so it can read old (item 747 did for about 15 minutes).
Based on (ruling): your item 593 a ruled the copy timely, not real time; PR #3212 stamps the copy with its age. This option goes beyond that ruling.
Based on (read): the retrospective's take: yes. The writer exports on that wake. No timer, no new process.
Departs from: main — the copy is exported when triage runs an export, with a stated age; option a exports at each Send.
Meanwhile: the stated age shows how old the copy is. Cost per Send (a few reads and one commit on the roadmap branch) is unmeasured.

options.gain: The copy is never older than your last save.
options.label: Yes: each Send wakes the writer, which exports the git copy then (recommended)
options.lose: A few reads and one commit per Send (unmeasured); many small commits on the roadmap branch.

options.gain: Fewer commits; no change to what you ruled.
options.label: No: keep the timely export and the stated age, as you ruled (item 593 a)
options.lose: The copy can read old for a while after a save.

short: Pressing Send on the page also exports the git copy?
title: Should your pressing Send on the waiting page also refresh the git copy of the page?
why: It changes when the git copy is written; you ruled it timely, not real time (item 593 a).
